The Persian Empire was one of the most powerful and influential states in the middle east for the last 100 years. They were the ones to invite the turkic raiders to settle in Syria, establishing a Persian vassal state there, and led to the end of Cappadocias domination of the Asia Minor region. Persia did however end up experiencing major political instability, partly due to the wars with the Rashidun, Egyptians and Armenians, partly due to overextension and partly due to a weak emperor. The Sultanate of Rum declared independence once the third Rum-Cappadocian war was finished, using their new lands to defeat the Persian armies. When the Persian Emperor died his heir was still a young child, leading to a power struggle that escalated into a fullblown civil war. The two remaining factions are the Shiite uprising, who wish for a more religious orientation with regards to governance, and the Qajar dynasty, led by Persian general to install himself on the throne. The future of the Empire hangs in the balance.
